title: Instagram self-harm alert to Madhya Pradesh cyber police leads Satna officers to a 17-year-old within about an hour; she is counseled and sent home (3 November 2022)
summary: 3 November 2022, about 5 pm: Instagram emailed MP cyber police a self-harm alert; Bhopal and Indore teams traced a 17-year-old to Satna in about an hour; she was counseled and sent home.
account: On 3 November 2022 at about 5 pm, Madhya Pradesh's state cyber police received an alert, emailed by Instagram's US office, that a user in the state had suffered a body injury; the Indore cyber-crime unit shared the “self-harm” alert with the cyber headquarters in Bhopal (ANI, 5 November 2022; Times of India, 4 November 2022). The girl, 17, had uploaded two videos, one with a packet of poison beside her as she behaved as if drunk and one in which she appeared to cut a vein (ANI); the Times of India mentions a small cut on her wrist. State Cyber SP Vaibhav Shrivastava said: “After an effort of one hour, we traced the location of the girl”, in Satna district, and Satna police were informed (ANI). Satna SP Ashutosh Gupta said officers located her and called her in with her mother; she said she only wanted to scare her boyfriend, and was sent home after counseling (Times of India).
purpose: Instagram's self-harm detection was built to flag content indicating self-harm or suicide risk and route alerts to agencies that can intervene; an alert that brought police to a girl posting self-harm videos was that purpose.
system: Instagram self-harm content detection and alert routing
deployer: Instagram; alert acted on by the Madhya Pradesh State Cyber Police (Bhopal headquarters and Indore unit) and Satna Police
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the good is a welfare check and counseling for a teen flagged for self-harm, with only a minor injury documented.

ratings.reason: A 17-year-old who had posted videos with poison and an apparent cut was reached and counseled within about an hour of the alert and sent home with a small cut on her wrist; by her own account she wanted to scare her boyfriend, so an averted suicide (4) rests on the police's framing and is not established.

ai_role.statement: Police say the alert came by email from Instagram's US office after the videos were posted; an ASP described the platform's AI algorithms as flagging non-graphic self-harm content such as scars, search words and hashtags, but no source says whether a classifier or a user report started the alert or whether Instagram staff reviewed it. Everything after the email was human work: Bhopal and Indore technical teams traced the location in about an hour, and Satna police found and counseled her.
